name: Dovetail
summary: A self-hostable home for customer interviews, evidence, synthesis, and durable research memory.
whyNow: Research archives contain unusually sensitive customer data, while enterprise access, governance, and AI analysis remain tied to a closed platform.
wedge: Lead with data ownership, lossless export, transcription, tags, clips, semantic search, and granular permissions—not broad AI parity.
ossLandscape: This review found no mature direct open-source research repository with Dovetail's integrated workflow.
recommendedMove: Create a clean-room flagship with two design partners and a security review before expanding scope.
risk: Permission depth, search quality, transcription accuracy, and enterprise migration can make the apparent MVP deceptively large.
milestones: Ship evidence tagging and semantic retrieval

name: Lattice
summary: The active build: an open performance system for 25–250 employee organizations with reversible reviews, inspectable permissions, and portable evidence.
whyNow: Per-seat modules and a minimum annual contract leave smaller teams with a meaningful cost and ownership incentive.
wedge: Start with review cycles, goals, evidence, one-to-ones, calibration, and exports while explicitly excluding payroll and full HRIS scope.
ossLandscape: Broad open HR systems exist, but few offer a focused modern replacement for the core Lattice workflow.
recommendedMove: Build the focused Performance replacement now, starting with the authenticated, tenant-isolated review-cycle spine.
risk: Employee data is sensitive, and review calibration plus organizational permissions require mature product judgment.
milestones: Model teams, cycles, goals, and permissions
Run a complete review and calibration cycle

name: Motion
priceSignal: $19–$29 per seat monthly on annual billing
summary: A deterministic open planner that turns tasks, calendars, and constraints into a realistic day.
whyNow: Commodity models can interpret intent, while a transparent constraint engine can own the scheduling decisions users need to trust.
wedge: Local-first tasks, Google and Microsoft calendar sync, explainable rescheduling, and optional bring-your-own model keys.
ossLandscape: No clearly mature and focused open-source equivalent surfaced in the research review.
recommendedMove: Run a 60-day greenfield challenge with reliability and cohort retention as the gates.
risk: Calendar edge cases, mobile polish, and loss of trust after one bad automatic reschedule.

name: Kajabi
summary: An integrated open creator stack spanning content, community, audience, checkout, and membership access.
whyNow: Creators pay a high integration premium even though credible open primitives exist for most individual capabilities.
wedge: A coherent installer, shared identity and entitlement model, migration tooling, and opinionated creator workflow.
ossLandscape: Courses, community, email, and checkout exist separately; the missing product is the cohesive operating layer.
recommendedMove: Assemble and harden existing primitives instead of rebuilding every subsystem.
risk: Payments, tax, email delivery, analytics, and migrations make the integration surface broad.

name: Canny
summary: The proving-ground mission: make Fider the easiest credible path away from closed product-feedback software.
whyNow: The product surface is bounded, migration value is obvious, and a mature self-hostable foundation already exists.
wedge: Canny import, public roadmap, changelog, SSO, integrations, accessible UI, and one-command deployment.
ossLandscape: Fider is AGPL, self-hostable, actively used, and already has a meaningful contributor base.
recommendedMove: Fund and harden Fider rather than fragment the category with another greenfield repository.
risk: A disconnected fork would create maintenance burden without improving the existing ecosystem.

name: Maze
priceSignal: Enterprise is quote-led; panel responses add cost
summary: An open testing workflow for prototypes, surveys, information architecture, and research analysis.
whyNow: The software layer is composable, while participant recruitment can remain a pluggable service rather than a hidden dependency.
wedge: Combine prototype testing and surveys with portable study data and bring-your-own participant sources.
ossLandscape: Quant-UX and Formbricks cover strong components but do not yet present one polished end-to-end replacement.
recommendedMove: Integrate existing projects and focus new work on study orchestration and migration.
risk: The participant network is a marketplace moat that open-source software alone cannot reproduce.
milestones: Define a shared study and response model
Run five studies without a closed panel

name: Gong
priceSignal: Per-user licenses plus a platform fee
summary: Self-hosted meeting capture and transparent revenue coaching built around open, inspectable signals.
whyNow: Large seat-based contracts and sensitive call data create a powerful self-hosting and cost wedge.
wedge: Build CRM-native scoring, coaching, review, and governance on top of proven meeting capture.
ossLandscape: Vexa already provides Apache-2.0 capture across Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom.
recommendedMove: Back Vexa and add the revenue workflow rather than rebuilding meeting infrastructure.
risk: Recording consent, meeting-platform changes, CRM breadth, and enterprise security are substantial.
milestones: Add structured sales signals and CRM sync
Run with one ten-seat sales team

name: Circle
priceSignal: $89–$199 per month before add-ons and fees
summary: A creator-owned community, course, event, and membership experience assembled from open foundations.
whyNow: Creators face software fees and transaction costs while strong community and course primitives already exist.
wedge: Unify creator onboarding, payments, entitlements, moderation, events, and migration across existing tools.
ossLandscape: Discourse and OpenCourse cover major pieces; the cohesive creator monetization layer remains open.
recommendedMove: Integrate the strongest projects and invest in migration plus mobile-quality experience.
risk: Payments, moderation, notifications, mobile expectations, and community migration are operationally demanding.
milestones: Map the community and course stack

name: Superhuman Mail
summary: A privacy-forward, local-first email client with fast keyboard workflows and transparent AI assistance.
whyNow: The premium price and sensitive data create a compelling ownership story, while several open clients show early momentum.
wedge: Local search, provider-agnostic sync, inspectable AI, and exceptional keyboard performance.
ossLandscape: Metis Mail, Zero, and other projects exist, but no polished winner clearly owns the category.
recommendedMove: Select and back the strongest client after a focused technical and maintainer review.
risk: OAuth approval, offline sync, security, provider quirks, and native-client polish are difficult to shortcut.

name: Vanta
summary: Open compliance automation with customer-controlled evidence, frameworks, connectors, and audit workflows.
whyNow: The category has an unusually large proven spend pool and a strong data-sovereignty argument.
wedge: Strengthen framework coverage, connectors, migration, deployment, and independently reviewed security.
ossLandscape: Openlane and other open-source challengers are already active in the category.
recommendedMove: Back Openlane or another credible maintainer; do not create a greenfield compliance platform.
risk: Security liability, framework maintenance, audit trust, integration breadth, and enterprise sales cycles are high.
milestones: Complete challenger security and governance review
